review_scope: Targeted literature and source review; not systematic and not a commercial production recipe.
numeric_parameter_policy: No publication record in this register independently authorizes a commercial crop coefficient. Numeric extraction requires endpoint, methods, units, applicability and independent verification.

documents.title: Light-Time-Biomass Response Model for Predicting the Growth of Choy Sum (Brassica rapa var. parachinensis) in Soil-Based LED-Constructed Indoor Plant Factory for Efficient Seedling Production
documents.scope: Singapore-affiliated; soil-based indoor LED; experiment details still require extraction
documents.finding: Models light, time and seedling biomass.
documents.design_implication: Nursery-stage growth-model candidate.
documents.limit: Seedling biomass is not mature marketable yield; extract stage and fresh/dry-weight definitions before parameterization.

documents.title: Widely-targeted metabolomics and transcriptomics identify metabolites associated with flowering regulation of Choy Sum
documents.scope: China; precise experimental site requires verification; flowering study
documents.finding: Investigates flowering-related physiology and molecular signals.
documents.design_implication: Motivates a flowering-stage and quality field.
documents.limit: Omics associations are not a validated days-to-harvest model.

documents.title: Optimal Plant Density, Nutrient Concentration and Rootzone Temperature for Higher Growth and Yield of Brassica rapa L. Curly Dwarf Pak Choy in Raft Hydroponic System Under Tropical Climate
documents.scope: Sabah, Malaysia; raft hydroponics
documents.finding: Tests density, solution conductivity and root-zone temperature jointly.
documents.design_implication: Require cultivar- and system-specific density and temperature interaction fields.
documents.limit: The best tested treatment is not a universal recipe; DOI was not established.

documents.title: Extended photoperiod improves growth and nutritional quality of pak choi under constant daily light integral
documents.scope: Netherlands; SFA co-author and funding; controlled-environment hydroponics
documents.finding: Three cultivars were compared across photoperiod and light-intensity treatments; final harvest was 32 days after sowing in that experiment.
documents.design_implication: Separate PPFD, photoperiod, DLI, cultivar and energy cost.
documents.limit: Constant DLI does not imply identical growth; the Zenodo deposit is described as LC-MS data, not necessarily a complete yield time series.

documents.title: Microclimate control to increase productivity and nutritional quality of leafy vegetables in a cost-effective manner
documents.scope: Singapore; aeroponics and tropical greenhouse
documents.finding: Discusses root-zone management and supplementary lighting in tropical production.
documents.design_implication: Represent protected systems, root-zone conditions and energy/water trade-offs.
documents.limit: Research overview; cited experiments must not be counted again as independent observations.

documents.title: Nitrate accumulation, productivity and photosynthesis of Brassica alboglabra grown under low light with supplemental LED lighting in the tropical greenhouse
documents.scope: Singapore; tropical greenhouse with supplementary LEDs
documents.finding: Examines light, productivity and nitrate accumulation.
documents.design_implication: Track marketable quality as well as biomass for kailan.
documents.limit: No universal nitrogen, nitrate-limit or LED prescription is inferred.

documents.title: Reduced nitrogen availability in hydroponically grown Chinese broccoli does not affect photosynthetic performance and yield while enhancing nitrogen use efficiency and nutritional quality
documents.scope: Singapore-affiliated; precise site to extract; hydroponics
documents.finding: Studies reduced nitrogen within a defined experimental treatment range.
documents.design_implication: Candidate nutrient-efficiency evidence with baseline and treatment context.
documents.limit: The year is 2026 despite a 2025 DOI suffix; this does not authorize autonomous fertilizer changes.

documents.title: Controlling root zone temperature improves plant growth and pigments in hydroponic lettuce
documents.scope: Japan; hydroponics
documents.finding: Root-zone temperature affects biomass and pigments under tested conditions.
documents.design_implication: Separate root temperature from air temperature in yield features.
documents.limit: Performance remains conditional on cultivar, ambient conditions and experimental scale.

documents.title: Raising root zone temperature improves plant productivity and metabolites in hydroponic lettuce production
documents.scope: Japan; hydroponics
documents.finding: Root warming can help in its tested environmental context.
documents.design_implication: Add a contradiction/context check when retrieving root-cooling literature.
documents.limit: Cooling and warming studies are not contradictory when baselines differ; there is no one fixed optimum.

documents.title: A short-term cooling of root-zone temperature increases bioactive compounds in baby leaf Amaranthus tricolor L.
documents.scope: Chiba, Japan; indoor hydroponic baby leaf
documents.finding: Examines short cooling treatments and quality/growth trade-offs.
documents.design_implication: Keep baby-leaf stage and quality target distinct from full-size bayam.
documents.limit: One non-Singapore experiment; do not optimize biomass with a quality-stress coefficient.

documents.title: Changes in Growth and Anthocyanin Content of Brassica juncea L. affected by Light Intensity and Photoperiod in Plant Factory with Artificial Lighting
documents.scope: Korea; indoor plant factory
documents.finding: Red mustard responds to lighting conditions in growth and pigmentation.
documents.design_implication: Use cultivar-specific light and quality features.
documents.limit: Red mustard results cannot automatically be assigned to all Chinese mustard cultivars.

documents.title: Effect of Light Quality on Physiological Disorder, Growth, and Secondary Metabolite Content of Water Spinach (Ipomoea aquatica Forsk) Cultivated in a Closed-type Plant Production System
documents.scope: Japan; closed hydroponic production
documents.finding: Light spectrum affects biomass allocation and intumescence injury.
documents.design_implication: Include marketable defect and packout endpoints, not only total biomass.
documents.limit: The full-text page states a non-commercial Creative Commons licence; commercial corpus redistribution is blocked.

documents.title: Growth and photosynthetic characteristics of sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) leaves grown under natural sunlight with supplemental LED lighting in a tropical greenhouse
documents.scope: Singapore; tropical greenhouse
documents.finding: Studies sweet-potato leaves rather than simply tuber production.
documents.design_implication: Build a leaf/shoot product model separate from tuber recipes.
documents.limit: Leaf biomass and regrowth scheduling require leaf-specific data.

documents.title: Plant Growth and Nutritional Quality Attributes of Basella alba Applied with Variable Rates of Nitrogen Fertilizer at Different Planting Dates under Canadian Maritime Climatic Conditions
documents.scope: Nova Scotia, Canada; outdoor field
documents.finding: Examines planting time and nitrogen under a maritime climate.
documents.design_implication: Capture season, trial location, plant part and fertilizer context for Basella.
documents.limit: Do not transfer Canadian dates or rates directly to Singapore; study quality needs assessment before numeric extraction.

documents.title: Effects of Temperature, Relative Humidity, and Carbon Dioxide Concentration on Growth and Glucosinolate Content of Kale Grown in a Plant Factory
documents.scope: Korea; plant factory
documents.finding: Evaluates environment and kale growth and quality responses.
documents.design_implication: Prioritize environment-by-cultivar feature collection.
documents.limit: Taxon and cultivar must be confirmed from full methods; do not conflate Chinese kale and curly kale.

documents.title: Using Machine Learning Models to Predict Hydroponically Grown Lettuce Yield
documents.scope: Egypt; greenhouse hydroponic and aeroponic systems
documents.finding: Compares ML methods using plant measurements recorded at harvest.
documents.design_implication: Model-candidate reference and forecast-leakage test case.
documents.limit: Harvest-time dry weight and contemporaneous measurements cannot be used in an earlier planting-date forecast.

documents.title: Lettuce Production in Intelligent Greenhouses—3D Imaging and Computer Vision for Plant Spacing Decisions
documents.scope: Bleiswijk, Netherlands; greenhouse
documents.finding: Links crop imaging to spacing decisions; companion experimental data exists.
documents.design_implication: Optional image-derived canopy and spacing features after baseline models.
documents.limit: External greenhouse data is not a representative Singapore farm-demand dataset.

documents.title: Effect of harvesting interval and defoliation on yield and chemical composition of leaves, stems and tubers of sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas L. (Lam.)) plant parts
documents.scope: Vietnam; field; multiple harvest regimes
documents.finding: Distinguishes leaf, stem and tuber responses to harvesting.
documents.design_implication: Motivates multi-cut regrowth and plant-part accounting.
documents.limit: Feed/biomass objectives and dry-matter results are not fresh-market saleable leaf yield.

documents.title: Limitations to photosynthesis of lettuce grown under tropical conditions: alleviation by root-zone cooling
documents.scope: Singapore; tropical cultivation with root-zone treatments
documents.finding: Contrasts cooled roots with fluctuating warm root-zone conditions.
documents.design_implication: Locally relevant physiological context for protected lettuce.
documents.limit: Older physiological experiment; not an energy-price or commercial yield forecast.

documents.title: Enhancing Productivity and Improving Nutritional Quality of Subtropical and Temperate Leafy Vegetables in Tropical Greenhouses and Indoor Farming Systems
documents.scope: Singapore-focused synthesis; protected and indoor systems
documents.finding: Synthesizes tropical controlled-environment research.
documents.design_implication: Seed backward and forward citation discovery and contextual comparisons.
documents.limit: A review is not another independent experimental dataset.

documents.title: Cultivation viability of Allium tuberosum L. in the Western Ghats: insights into crop dynamics, yield and quality
documents.scope: Rajgurunagar, India; black-soil raised beds; three accessions observed across two years with repeated foliage cuts
documents.finding: Accessions and seasonal windows differed in foliage growth and harvest quality; greater tillering and spread accompanied both higher foliage yield and more harvest waste in this experiment.
documents.design_implication: Represent accession, season, crop age, cut number, saleable foliage and waste separately for a perennial repeated-cut crop.
documents.limit: A warm Indian field trial with mature mother material does not establish Singapore hydroponic yield, spacing, harvest interval or profitability.

documents.title: Physiological, transcriptomic, and metabolic analyses reveal that mild salinity improves the growth, nutrition, and flavor properties of hydroponic Chinese chive (Allium tuberosum Rottler ex Spr)
documents.scope: Beijing, China; one named Chinese-chive cultivar in a controlled hydroponic salinity experiment
documents.finding: The tested salinity treatments changed growth, mineral composition, metabolites and flavour-related compounds, demonstrating that biomass and quality endpoints can move differently.
documents.design_implication: Keep salinity, cultivar, biomass, mineral composition and sensory or flavour proxies as distinct observations.
documents.limit: A short controlled stress experiment on one cultivar is not a nutrient recipe or proof that salinity improves saleable output under Singapore farm conditions.

documents.title: Effect of shade and sowing method on Eryngium foetidum production
documents.scope: Gazipur and Magura, Bangladesh; split-plot comparison of three shade environments and two sowing methods over 2012–2014
documents.finding: Shade environment and sowing method affected leaf-production timing and measured yield, with effects evaluated at two tropical field locations.
documents.design_implication: Record shade structure, sowing method, location, season, flowering and fresh-leaf endpoint together.
documents.limit: The tested Bangladesh systems and reported field yields do not establish a Singapore recipe, hydroponic response or buyer-grade packout.

documents.title: Amazon chicory: growing at full sunlight or under shade?
documents.scope: Capanema, Para, Brazil; field comparison of full sun and graded shading for Eryngium foetidum
documents.finding: Graded shade treatments changed leaf-area, biomass and production endpoints, showing that shade response should be modeled as treatment- and endpoint-specific.
documents.design_implication: Preserve actual irradiance or shade treatment and distinguish leaf fresh mass, dry mass, area and marketable yield.
documents.limit: One equatorial Brazilian experiment cannot resolve Singapore cultivar, infrastructure, season, economics or a universal shade target.
